entry.name: ActionSense
entry.title: ActionSense: A Multimodal Dataset and Recording Framework for Human Activities Using Wearable Sensors in a Kitchen Environment
entry.summary: Kitchen activities in a mock kitchen with bimanual 32x32 conductive-thread tactile gloves, Manus bend-sensor finger tracking, Xsens body IMUs, Myo forearm EMG, Pupil Core eye tracking, 5 static RGB cameras and 2 microphones.
entry.hand: human hands wearing custom open-finger tactile gloves (conductive threads on a piezoresistive film) under Manus Prime II Xsens finger-tracking gloves

sensor.note: One sample per hand = 32x32 matrix of raw ADC readings (float32, 1,024 thread intersections); threads routed to a 23x19 palm grid, 5x9 thumb, 11x4 little finger and 13x4 on each other finger. Open-finger gloves: no fingertips. No matrix-to-hand-location map in the released files.

scale.text: ~13 h recorded (778 min; 543.5 min of activities), 574 labeled activity instances (9 subjects), 20 activities, 10 subjects, 1 mock kitchen; tactile on 6 subjects (S00-S05)

entry.access: Open HTTP download, no login: per-subject HDF5 (wearables), MP4/AVI (eye-tracking world video), AVI + timestamp TXT (5 RGB cameras) and WAV (microphones) linked from action-sense.csail.mit.edu/data.html; HTTP range requests supported.
caveats: Tactile and finger tracking only for S00-S05; S06-S09 wore no tactile or finger-tracking gloves (their HDF5 files have no tactile-glove groups and only 23 Xsens segments).
S01: wearable data was lost after calibration and peeling cucumbers; its HDF5 holds only calibration plus 3 labeled activities.
Tactile is about 6 Hz in practice (the sensor table on the website lists 15 Hz).

Tactile is raw ADC counts with no conversion to force; the scale calibration periods (Dymo M25 weight_g) are provided for that. Metadata says range [0, 4095], but released values lie in 23..1023 with a ~560 resting baseline.
Tactile response during activities is small: the 20 most-loaded cells typically sit 10-150 counts above baseline.
The HDF5 tactile streams carry no map from the 32x32 matrix to palm/finger regions.
Finger tracking: the data page warns the Manus gloves may not have worked reliably; the Manus IMUs were disabled, so there is no lateral finger spread.
Depth camera data and the external RGB/audio for S06-S09 are listed as 'coming soon' on the data page; raw FLIR frames are not linked (only AVI videos).
Recordings are continuous per subject (1-4 splits); activities are Start/Stop label rows in experiment-activities, not separate files.
Label names vary across subjects (e.g. 'Get items from refrigerator/cabinets/drawers' vs 'Get/replace items ...').

tracking.note: 60 Hz; segment poses, joint angles, CoM, foot contacts; streamed live from MVN, with scripts to merge re-processed MVN estimates
bend sensors, glove IMUs disabled (finger curl only); finger segments arrive through the Xsens stream at 60 Hz (63 segments / 60 joints instead of 23 / 22); site warns finger data may be unreliable
hand segment pose from the body suit; Myo armbands also give forearm orientation (arbitrary reference frame)

other: forearm EMG (Myo armband, 8 ch per arm, ~200 Hz)
eye tracking / gaze and pupil geometry (Pupil Core, ~115 Hz)
Dymo M25 scale weight readings for tactile calibration

sources: https://data.csail.mit.edu/ActionNet/wearable_data/ (all 19 wearable HDF5 files: tree, attributes, rates and tactile values read with HTTP range requests)
unconfirmed: hours = 778.0 min total (includes calibration routines) / 60; activity time alone is 543.5 min (~9.1 h). Tactile streams in the release add up to ~24,570 s (~6.8 h) over the 12 HDF5 files of S00-S05 (left glove time_s spans).

episodes = 574 labeled activity instances over 9 subjects (website activity_stats table, 324.26 min). Pairing Start/Stop rows in the released files gives 586 instances (306 in S00-S05 incl. 3 for S01, 280 in S06-S09) and ~329 min.
frames: tactile frames in the release = 144,404 (left) + 142,048 (right) over S00-S05, counted from the HDF5 tactile_data shapes.
Tactile rate: website sensor table 15 Hz; supplement HDF5 table '6 [improveable to ~15]'; measured 4.5-6.2 Hz per file (time_s), 6.0-6.1 Hz in activity splits.
Egocentric world camera resolution 1280x720 MJPEG, ~29.6 fps: ffprobe of S05 world_frame.mp4 / worldGaze_frame.avi; not stated in the paper.
FLIR AVI videos are MPEG-4 Part 2, 1600x1200, 22 fps (ffprobe of S05 PG1); one timestamp line per frame in the PG*.txt files.

Subjects with tactile: data page says S06-S09 had no gloves; supplement says 'the last 5 subjects'; S01 has tactile only for calibration and 3 activities. The files confirm tactile groups in S00-S05 and none in S06-S09.
taxels_per_hand 682 = 23x19 + 5x9 + 11x4 + 3x(13x4), computed from the stated grids; the file stores all 1,024 matrix intersections.

Released tactile values never exceed 1023 in any of the 12 files although the stream metadata says [0, 4095] (TouchStreamer.py hard-codes that range); how the 32 thread rows/cols map to the hand regions is not documented.
subjects = 10 (data page and supplement); 70% male, 90% right-handed, 27.3 +- 3.7 years.

download.format: Per subject and recording split: one HDF5 file of all wearable streams (device group > stream group > data, time_s, time_str), eye-tracking world video as MJPEG .mp4 (no overlay) and .avi (gaze overlay), 5 FLIR camera .avi (MPEG-4) + per-frame timestamp .txt, 2 microphone .wav + an HDF5 of chunk timestamps; XLSX/PDF surveys.
download.total_size: ~465 GB for the 182 linked files (sum of Content-Length): wearable HDF5 0.17-4.3 GB each (19 files, 39.1 GB), eye-tracking videos 0.75-24 GB each, FLIR AVIs 0.5-3.0 GB each, WAVs 0.2-0.7 GB each
download.per_episode: Tactile for one 30 s activity (both hands, float32) is ~1.5 MB of the HDF5; the whole split's HDF5 is 0.25-4.3 GB, egocentric video for the split 2-24 GB, each FLIR camera 0.5-3 GB.
download.partial_fetch: data.csail.mit.edu serves Accept-Ranges: bytes; h5py over an HTTP range-reading file object reads metadata, labels and the tactile arrays of one split for ~20-270 MB of transfer. MP4/AVI can be cut by byte range only roughly (no index for AVI); ffprobe/ffmpeg read them over HTTP.

episodes.scene: MIT CSAIL mock kitchen (the only scene)
episodes.subject: S00
episodes.why: Pour, one hand: the right hand holds the pitcher. Figures are the converter's: mean of the 20 most raised thread crossings above rest on the 30 Hz episode clock, suspected faulty crossings left out (see checks.faulty_cells). Right glove +94 on average (peak +135), above +30 for 9.3 s of 10.1 s (longest run 9.3 s); left glove at rest (+9, peak +15). The longest pour instance in the release; all others are 4-10 s. With the faulty right-glove crossings (21, 31), (22, 31) included the right glove would read +129 (peak +172).

sample.fetch_estimate: ~2.5 GB of range reads, nothing near a whole file: wearable HDF5 ~50-100 MB per split for metadata, labels and the window's arrays (5 splits, ~0.5 GB); egocentric world MP4 (MJPEG, ~5.6 MB/s from file size / split duration) for 207 s of windows, ~1.2 GB; 5 FLIR AVIs at ~0.4-0.65 MB/s each for 207 s, ~0.6 GB plus index reads; WAV 48 kHz 16-bit mono ~0.1 MB/s x 2 mics, ~40 MB. Whole files would be 0.5-21 GB each (the 5 splits' world MP4s alone are ~80 GB).
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 20 activities (> 6), so 7 taken, spanning action types (pour, twist, wipe, spread, slice, peel, pick and place), objects (pitcher, jar, pan, bread, cucumber, potato, dishes) and one- vs two-handed use; there is one kitchen, so scenes cannot vary. Fetching items, clearing the cutting board and stacking/setting the table were left out as near-duplicates of the dishwasher pick and place. Episodes: one per task, 7 in total, from 5 subjects (S00, S02, S03, S04 x2, S05 x2); only S00-S05 have tactile, and S01 was excluded because its wearable data stops after 3 activities. Episode = one labelled activity instance: id = <subject>_<split file time>_act<NNN>, where NNN is the 0-based index of the instance in the list built by pairing Start/Stop rows of experiment-activities/activities in file order; label_epoch_s holds the paired time_s values. All 7 are rated 'Good' with empty notes. Length: 6 instances are 8.5-53.3 s and kept whole (window null); the dishwasher instance (155.8 s) is cut to a 45 s window, given in seconds after the label start. Contact rule: 'rest' = per-cell median over the instance +-150 s; a frame is in contact when the mean of the 20 most-raised cells exceeds rest by 30 counts (its median over each whole split is 5-22 counts). Applied with the suspected faulty crossings (checks.faulty_cells) left out, every episode has a run of at least 2.1 s above it on at least one glove (S03 spread 2.1 s, S04 jar 3.1 s on the left glove at only +27 on average: weak contact, see its why; all others 4.6-35 s). Channels: both gloves present in every window, no NaN, no constant cells, 63-329 frames per glove at 5.8-6.3 Hz, max frame gap 0.22 s. Budget: tactile for the longest window is ~2.7 MB as float32 and must be quantised (counts are integers 0-1023, so uint16 or offsets from rest) to keep the episode JSON under 2 MB; video must be re-encoded (1280x720 MJPEG at ~5.6 MB/s and 1600x1200 MPEG-4) to stay under ~30 MB per episode.

checks.method: HDF5 read over HTTP range requests with h5py (scripts: scratchpad/scripts/ac/check_eps.py); FLIR coverage from the first and last lines of each split's PG1 timestamp .txt
checks.tactile_channels: tactile-glove-left/tactile_data and tactile-glove-right/tactile_data present in all 5 files and covering every window (see each episode's why).
checks.tactile_calibration_scale: tactile-calibration-scale/weight_g present in all 5 files (758-3,388 readings per file) but with 0 readings inside any sampled window: the scale is used only during the calibration periods, not during activities.
checks.experiment_calibration_tactile_gloves: Present in all 5 files; 2-46 label rows, except S02 split 22-35-11, whose tactile_gloves dataset has 0 rows (S02's glove calibration is in its 21-48-24 and 23-22-44 splits).
checks.xsens_foot_contacts: foot_contact_points present for every window (60 Hz, e.g. 607 frames for the 10.1 s pour); foot-ground, not hand touch.
checks.finger_tracking: xsens-segments/position_cm has 63 segments (23 body + 40 finger) in all 5 files, no NaN inside the windows.
checks.hot_cells: Superseded by faulty_cells. An earlier version of this check said that right-glove (21, 31) and (22, 31) sit at ~1016-1018 throughout the S00 pour and S04 slice windows and are part of the rest level; that was wrong. Their rest (median over the episode +-150 s) is 564-567 in S00 act026, S00 act028, S04 act007 and S05 act058, and they read ~+450 whenever they toggle high; only in S02 act016 and S03 act002 is their median ~1016-1018.
checks.saturation: No sampled window has working crossings pinned at 1023 except 5 samples in the S03 spread window (right glove). Left-glove pan cleaning in S00 and S03 saturates (top-20 cells ~+460 = 1023), which is why S02 was used.
checks.external_coverage: FLIR PG1 timestamps cover every window: S00 1654639864-1654643524, S02 1655174091-1655175101, S03 1655229133-1655231218, S04 1655239017-1655242784, S05 (single external split from 20:35:06) 1655253318-1655257573. Egocentric world_frame.mp4 exists for all 5 splits.
checks.faulty_cells: Right-glove crossings (21, 31), (22, 31) [distal end of the band assumed to be the index finger] and (21, 11), (21, 12), (22, 11), (22, 12) [palm] are two-state: over each episode +-150 s their samples sit either at rest (~565) or at ~1000-1023 (mostly ~1018), with almost none between 700 and 950, while the neighbouring crossings rise by at most ~+15 counts when they are high (e.g. S04 act007 (21, 31): 37 samples < 700, 0 in 700-950, 187 > 950 in the 38.5 s window). Pressure on the film would pass through the middle range and raise the neighbours, so they are taken as intermittent read-out faults. Rule (converter faulty_cells, per episode over the +-150 s span): >= max(10, 0.5 %) of samples above 950, at most 1/5 as many in 700-950, the largest median rise of non-flagged neighbouring crossings while high < 20 counts, and not high together with more than 3 crossings of its own matrix row. Flagged per episode: S00 act028 and S04 act007 / act032: (21, 31), (22, 31); S02 act016 and S05 act058: (21, 12), (22, 12), (21, 31), (22, 31) (in S02 the two col-31 cells sit at ~1018 for 69 % / 99.5 % of the span); S03 act002: all six ((22, 31) is at ~1018 throughout, (21, 31) 69 %); S05 act012: none. Over the whole S04 session (both gloves, 22,000 frames each) the rule flags only right (21, 31), (22, 31); the left glove has none in any sampled episode. Flagged crossings are drawn hollow ('inactive') and left out of the region sums, the top-20 contact metric and the colour range; each episode's notes name them with their share of high samples. The faulty cells inflated the earlier top-20 figures: e.g. S00 pour right 130 -> 94, S04 slice 101 -> 66, S03 spread 81 -> 31, S05 dishwasher 30 -> 22, and the old S00 jar episode from 34 (13.3 s above +30) to 12 (0.2 s).
checks.line_bursts: Left glove S02 22-35-11 (and S03 13-52-57 outside the crossings): single frames in which a run of 6-7 entries of one matrix row reads ~1018 (rows 0, 3, 28, 29, cols 22-28; 46 frames over the S02 episode +-150 s), a read-out fault; none falls inside a sampled episode. The non-crossing entries (28, 24)-(28, 28) and (29, 25) toggle the same way inside the S02 episode; they are not drawn and the notes say so.

visualization.detail: 682 thread crossings on a 33x33 hand layout (palm 23x19, thumb 9x5 drawn sideways at the lower palm, index/middle/ring 4x13, little 4x11), counts above per-cell rest (median over the instance +-150 s), stored at the native ~6 Hz with a clock index; per-region sums and the mean of the 20 most raised cells plotted. Placement derived from the data (non-crossing entries barely respond), finger order and distal end assumed; 342 non-crossing matrix entries not drawn. Crossings flagged as faulty by the converter's faulty_cells rule (bimodal rest/~1018 with quiet neighbours) are drawn as hollow 'inactive' squares and left out of the sums, the top-20 plot and the colour range; none on the left glove in the sampled episodes

same as left, mirrored (thumb on the left); suspected faulty crossings (21, 31), (22, 31), (21, 11), (21, 12), (22, 11), (22, 12), as flagged per episode, drawn hollow and left out of the sums, the top-20 plot and the colour range
